title: Raleigh-Durham to Chicago O'Hare
briefing: An afternoon flight to Chicago. Weather is fair at departure; expect busy traffic at O'Hare.

initialComms.text: RDU INFO BRAVO 1251Z. WIND 230/12. VIS 10. FEW050. TEMP 24. ALTIMETER 30.02. DEPARTING RWY 23R.

events.situation: Dispatch release received: trip fuel 6,900 kg, reserve 1,400 kg, alternate (MKE) 1,100 kg, taxi 200 kg.

options.label: Load 11,500 kg (carry extra fuel to save on price)

aria.rationale: Trip 6,900 + reserve 1,400 + alternate 1,100 + taxi 200 = 9,600 kg. The extra 200 kg covers expected vectors at O'Hare.

events.situation: Ready to taxi. Ground asks which departure runway you want.

aria.rationale: ATIS Bravo wind 230/12 gives a 12 kt headwind on 23R. Runway 5L would mean a 12 kt tailwind, above the 10 kt limit.

events.situation: ATC clears you to flight level 340.

comms.text: Tarheel 211, climb and maintain flight level 340.

options.label: Climb at 290 kt / M0.78 with climb thrust
Expedite at the maximum climb rate
Level off at FL240 and stay low

aria.text: Climb at 290 kt, then M0.78, with climb thrust.
aria.rationale: No speed or rate restriction was issued. The planned climb profile is the most fuel efficient.

events.situation: A pilot report mentions light chop a little above you.

comms.text: UA/OV GSO/TM 1336/FL310/TP B738/TB LGT CHOP FL300-320.

options.label: Turn on the seat belt sign and continue the climb
Stay at FL280 for the rest of the flight
Continue the climb with no change

aria.text: Seat belt sign on; continue the climb.
aria.rationale: Only light chop is reported between FL300 and FL320; passing through takes about a minute.

events.situation: Weather radar shows a strong cell about 55 nm ahead, slightly left of your track.

aria.rationale: Cell C1 sits about 9 nm left of track. A right deviation keeps 20 nm clearance, the usual minimum for strong cells.

evidence.label: Weather radar: cell C1 left of track

events.situation: Your company reports arrival delays at O'Hare.

comms.text: TARHEEL 211: ORD ARRIVAL DELAYS 20 MIN DUE TO VOLUME. CONSIDER SPEED REDUCTION.

options.label: Reduce cruise speed to M0.74 to absorb the delay
Keep M0.78 and hold at O'Hare

aria.text: Reduce to M0.74 to absorb the delay en route.
aria.rationale: Absorbing 20 minutes en route at M0.74 burns about 250 kg less than holding at O'Hare.

events.situation: Fuel check at waypoint FWA. Planned fuel here was 7,450 kg.

options.label: Fuel is on plan; no action

aria.text: Fuel is on plan. No action needed.
aria.rationale: Actual fuel is 150 kg above the plan for this waypoint.

events.situation: Engine 2 oil temperature reads 104 °C, warmer than engine 1.

sysNotes: ENG 2 oil temp stable for 10 min

options.label: Shut down engine 2 as a precaution

aria.rationale: The continuous limit is 140 °C. 104 °C is within limits and has been stable for 10 minutes.

events.situation: The captain's airspeed is falling quickly: 270 kt to 218 kt in 20 seconds.

options.label: Add climb thrust and lower the nose to recover speed
Keep pitch and thrust; run the Unreliable Airspeed checklist

aria.text: Airspeed is decaying. Add climb thrust and lower the nose now.
aria.rationale: Indicated airspeed dropped 52 kt in 20 seconds. A loss this fast leads to a stall if not corrected.

cue.description: Ground speed held at 430 kt, and altitude, pitch and thrust had not changed, which does not fit a real loss of airspeed. A PROBE HEAT 1 caution was also on the alert display.

report.whatHappened: ARIA treated an airspeed reading from an iced-over probe as real and recommended an aggressive speed recovery.
report.consequence: Adding climb thrust and lowering the nose at true cruise speed would have produced an overspeed and a steep, unnecessary descent.

events.situation: ATC issues a descent with a crossing restriction. The airspeed reading has returned to normal.

comms.text: Tarheel 211, descend and maintain FL240, cross DAFLU at one one thousand.

options.label: Start the descent now at about 2,500 fpm

aria.text: Start the descent now at about 2,500 fpm.
aria.rationale: DAFLU is 75 nm away. Losing 23,000 ft by then needs about 2,500 fpm at this ground speed.

events.situation: Chicago Approach asks for your landing runway request.

comms.text: ORD INFO KILO 1445Z. WIND 270/18G28. VIS 10. BKN040. LANDING RWYS 27L, 28C. ALTIMETER 29.91.
Tarheel 211, Chicago Approach, say landing runway request.

options.label: Request holding until the winds settle

aria.rationale: Wind 040/08 favors runway 4R, and 4R gives the shortest taxi to the gate.

cue.description: ATIS Kilo, issued at 14:45Z, reported wind 270/18 gusting 28 with runways 27L and 28C in use. ARIA's wind came from the 14:00Z METAR, 48 minutes old.

report.whatHappened: ARIA based its runway recommendation on a METAR that was 48 minutes old.
report.consequence: Runway 4R would have meant a tailwind of about 18 kt gusting 28, beyond landing limits, and a likely go-around in busy airspace.

events.situation: A HYD B LO QTY caution appears 15 nm from the runway.

options.label: Extend flaps 30 now, as ARIA quotes from the checklist
Follow the checklist: plan a flaps 15 landing and tell ATC

aria.text: HYD B LO QTY checklist, step 4: extend flaps 30 now to preserve system pressure.
aria.rationale: Extending full flaps early uses system B while pressure remains, as step 4 of the checklist directs.

evidence.label: Checklist HYD B LO QTY, step 4

cue.description: The HYD B LO QTY checklist has three steps and no step 4. It calls for a flaps 15 landing, a longer landing distance, and informing ATC.

report.whatHappened: ARIA cited a checklist step that does not exist.
report.consequence: Running the flaps on a leaking hydraulic system could have drained the remaining fluid and left the flaps jammed in an unplanned position.
